items.titleEn: 2 stocks to buy and 1 to sell as Democrats push for control of Congress
items.summaryEn: Buy HCA. The article ties a ~$400M Q3 pretax hit to uninsured losses after exchange coverage declines, while admissions and revenue are already rising. A Democratic shift raises odds of Medicaid/coverage concessions during fiscal negotiations, which directly improves payment economics for the same demand base. Catalyst is policy relief showing up in uninsured volumes and reimbursement trends. Key Risk: Coverage talks fail and uninsured volumes/reimbursement pressure keep worsening, wiping out the earnings rebound. Americans are voting today, with control of Congress and the next round of battles over healthcare, energy incentives, and federal spending, at stake.

items.titleEn: Why is this data center components supplier stock gaining 8% in premarket today?
items.summaryEn: Buy FN. The stock is up on record revenue (+51% YoY), record EPS, and a big upside data-center mix (53% of revenue; +78% YoY). Guidance calls for Q2 revenue $1.6–$1.65B and EPS $4.77–$4.92, both above consensus, plus margin strength (gross margin 12.1%). Capacity expansion is massive (Santa Clara +$300M, Nava 1 +$400M, Thailand Building 10 +$3.5B), supporting multi-quarter growth and buyback support ($200M remaining). Key Risk: AI/data-center optical demand slows faster than Fabrinet can ramp capacity, causing margins and guidance to roll over. Sell a lagging optical-packaging/connector peer basket (e.g., short a lower-quality optical components name like II-VI/II-VI-style optics exposure) versus FN. The news shows FN is winning with data-center optical packaging and interconnects plus clear capacity additions and stronger guidance. If the market rotates toward the best execution/ramp story, weaker peers with less credible capacity or margins get de-rated even if their results are merely “okay.”

items.titleEn: Oracle stock could be in trouble as an alarming pattern forms as dilution continues
items.summaryEn: Buy a basket that benefits from AI capex without the same dilution/debt overhang—specifically go long Microsoft (MSFT) and/or Amazon (AMZN) and short ORCL. Second-order angle: ORCL’s financing stress can shift enterprise AI spending away from Oracle’s stack toward hyperscalers that can fund AI internally, so the relative winners are the cash-rich platforms while ORCL absorbs the “funding overhang” discount. Key Risk: Oracle’s cloud/AI execution accelerates fast enough that customers don’t reallocate spend, and ORCL’s relative underperformance reverses despite the financing. Sell ORCL. The news is a clear dilution + leverage cycle: ~$10B new shares plus ~$10B senior notes, debt up to ~$169B, and the stock is breaking down technically (head-and-shoulders, below all moving averages, below Ichimoku/Supertrend). Even with revenue growth, the market is punishing the balance-sheet math and the AI backlog risk tied to OpenAI. Thesis: dilution and financing pressure keep compressing per-share value while technicals invite momentum selling toward ~$100 support; confirmation is a break below ~$115.2.

items.titleEn: Why Palantir shares are crashing despite strong third-quarter beat?
items.summaryEn: Buy Palantir (PLTR). The earnings beat is real: revenue first time above $2B, US commercial revenue now leads US government, and guidance for 2026 implies ~91% growth. The selloff is driven by TCV deceleration (new contract value), which often reflects contract timing/longer deal cycles rather than demand collapse. If revenue and free cash flow keep compounding, the market will re-rate the stock even if TCV growth is temporarily slower. Key Risk: US commercial bookings (TCV) keeps slowing for multiple quarters, proving demand is actually weakening and revenue growth is about to decelerate. Sell Palantir (PLTR) if you can trade around volatility. The market is punishing the gap between fast revenue growth and slower new contract growth (TCV +6% vs 49% prior quarter). Until US commercial TCV re-accelerates, the stock can stay under pressure despite beats, because investors are now focused on bookings quality and sustainability.

items.titleEn: Nasdaq 100 and QQQ have sunk into a correction: will they rebound after midterms?
items.summaryEn: Buy QQQ. The Nasdaq 100 is already down >10% from October highs, broke key support (~28,123), and RSI is near oversold—classic setup for a relief bounce. The article also flags a common pattern: tech/indices often sell into elections and then rebound after the midterms, especially if regulation fears fade. Key Risk: A sustained AI earnings/impairment wave keeps pressure on the whole index and prevents any rebound. Sell INTC. The stock is down ~51% in 30 days after earnings showed slowing business, and the market is treating AI exposure as a bubble risk. With AI-neocloud players facing potential collapses/impairments, Intel’s near-term demand and sentiment likely stay weak even if the index bounces.

items.titleEn: Nvidia tells data center partners to limit China exposure below 50%: report
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. If partners must keep China below 50%, Nvidia shifts demand toward non-China hyperscalers and model builders, supporting higher utilization and steadier revenue mix as export friction rises. The “not for existing contracts” detail implies near-term continuity plus incremental share gains elsewhere. Key Risk: US export rules tighten further and directly cap Nvidia’s ability to sell into China even for non-China partners’ supply chains, cutting total addressable demand. Buy Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN). Nvidia’s guidance pushes clouds to diversify away from China-heavy workloads, which favors global platforms with large non-China footprints and compliance teams. Expect incremental AI capacity demand and longer-term customer stickiness as customers re-route workloads to compliant regions.

items.titleEn: Why are Nvidia, AMD and Intel stocks rising in pre-market trading today?
items.summaryEn: Buy Nvidia (NVDA). The sell-off looks valuation-driven, not demand-driven: data-center revenue is already $89B (+117%) and management still guides to ~$108B for the next quarter. Pre-market strength signals bargain buyers are stepping in ahead of the Nov 17 print; if guidance holds, the stock can re-rate quickly because AI capex hasn’t actually broken yet. Key Risk: Cloud customers pause or slow AI data-center spending, forcing a guidance cut or margin compression. Buy AMD (AMD). It’s the highest-upside setup into earnings: revenue expected ~$13.1B (+42%) and investors will focus on whether server/AI accelerators can offset PC weakness. The stock is already bouncing, and a beat/raised data-center outlook would validate diversification away from a single AI-chip supplier and drive multiple expansion.

items.titleEn: Nvidia orders data center clients to reduce China exposure: FT
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: U.S. chipmaking giant Nvidia is ordering its data center partners to scale back work with Chinese customers, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. Nvidia's cloud computing clients must now sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies, the FT reported, citing five people with knowledge of the matter.

items.titleEn: MRVL, LITE stocks downgraded as merger raises dilution and limited-upside concerns
items.summaryEn: Buy Lumentum (LITE). The stock is being marked down mainly because MRVL is down, not because LITE’s standalone fundamentals collapsed. The exchange ratio (4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share) mechanically links LITE to MRVL, creating a valuation dislocation. If the market overreacts to dilution fears and the optical cycle holds, LITE can re-rate as the “standalone value + deal value” argument gains traction. Key Risk: China approval goes against the deal or forces harsh concessions that materially reduce the implied value (or the deal breaks), leaving LITE stuck with limited upside. Sell Marvell (MRVL). The all-stock deal is a clear EPS-dilution overhang (roughly 50% share-count dilution; mid-single-digit EPS dilution in 2028) with execution and regulatory timing risk. Analysts also flag possible customer/channel conflicts and that $1B cost saves likely won’t offset dilution. If optical transceiver demand disappoints after an industry mini-cycle peak, margins get hit right when the market expects accretion.

items.titleEn: 6 stocks Jim Cramer says are worth buying as AI stocks tumble
items.summaryEn: Buy RL. The stock has already proven demand for premium product (14% revenue growth; strong direct sales) and the Asia expansion story is working. The setup is a “quality rebound” within apparel as AI money rotates into consumer names, with RL positioned at the premium end where pricing power matters. Catalyst is Thursday’s fiscal Q2 print to confirm the current growth rate isn’t just a one-quarter spike. Key Risk: Earnings beat but guidance disappoints—investors decide the 380% rally already priced in a sustained premium-demand cycle. Buy KTB. The Lee sale is a value unlock, but the real edge is what management does next: deploy proceeds into buybacks and shareholder returns while focusing the portfolio on Wrangler/Helly Hansen. With ~14x earnings and ~3% dividend, the stock can re-rate if the market believes capital returns will be sustained, not just a one-time disposal.
